q1.question: What is local SEO and how does it differ from regular SEO?
q1.answer: Local SEO is search engine optimisation specifically for location-based searches - like 'plumber in Sofia' or 'dentist near me'. Unlike traditional SEO that targets standard organic results, local SEO focuses on the 'map pack' - the three businesses displayed on Google Maps. These searches have the highest buyer intent of any search type.

q2.question: What is Google Business Profile and do I need one?
q2.answer: Google Business Profile (GBP) is the free business listing that controls how your company appears on Google Maps and Search. Without a verified and optimised GBP, it is virtually impossible to rank in the Top 3. It is the foundation of everything we do - without it, even the best optimisation cannot work.

q3.question: Do I need a website to rank on Google Maps?
q3.answer: Not strictly required, but strongly recommended. A website sends additional authority signals to Google. Our Standard and Quarterly packages include full website optimisation. If you don't have a website, we can still help - but results will be significantly stronger with one.

q1.question: What exactly does your service include?
q1.answer: Every package includes: full competitor analysis, Google Business Profile optimisation (categories, attributes, photos, description, Q&A), high-quality citation and authority signal building, and bi-weekly updates. The Standard and Quarterly packages also include full website optimisation.

q2.question: Can you help us get more Google reviews?
q2.answer: Yes. We provide proven strategies and templates for collecting reviews without violating Google's policies. Reviews are a key ranking signal - more quality reviews directly improve your position in the map pack and build trust with potential customers.

q3.question: Which industries do you work with?
q3.answer: We work with any local business that serves customers face-to-face: plumbers, dentists, lawyers, accountants, auto repair shops, restaurants, hotels, beauty salons, gyms, and many more. If your customers search for businesses like yours on Google - we can help.

q4.question: What happens after the initial 90-day period?
q4.answer: Once you have reached the Top 3, we work to maintain and strengthen your position. The competitive landscape shifts over time - regular maintenance ensures you stay ahead. You can continue month-to-month or switch to the quarterly plan with a built-in discount.

q1.question: How quickly will we see movement in rankings?
q1.answer: Most clients see initial movement within 4–6 weeks. For the guaranteed Top 3 placement on the Standard and Quarterly packages - 90 days. Speed depends on niche competitiveness and your profile's current state.

q2.question: How do you track and report progress?
q2.answer: We monitor your Google Maps ranking weekly using specialist tools. You receive bi-weekly updates with concrete data on your ranking position, impressions, and user actions - calls, direction requests, and website visits.

q3.question: What if our competitors are also doing local SEO?
q3.answer: Competitor analysis is the first step of our process. We know exactly what the top-ranking businesses are doing and how to outpace their strategy. In 9 out of 10 cases, our clients reach the Top 3 even when competitors are actively investing in local SEO.

q4.question: What are citations and why do they matter?
q4.answer: A citation is any online mention of your business that includes your name, address, and phone number (NAP). Google uses the consistency and quality of these mentions as a trust signal. We build high-quality citations in authoritative, industry-specific directories relevant to your location.

q1.question: How exactly does the money-back guarantee work?
q1.answer: For the Standard and Quarterly packages: if we do not achieve a Top 3 ranking for the agreed keyword within 90 days, you receive a full refund of all amounts paid. The guarantee applies provided you granted us the required access on time and did not make changes to your profile without our knowledge.

q2.question: Are there any hidden setup fees or additional costs?
q2.answer: None. The price you see is everything you pay. No setup fees, no hidden add-ons, no performance charges. The monthly fee covers all work - analysis, optimisation, citations, and updates.

q3.question: Can I upgrade or switch plans later?
q3.answer: Yes. If you decide to move from Minimum to Standard, or switch to quarterly billing - just get in touch. The price difference is calculated on a pro-rata basis with no penalties.

q4.question: What payment methods do you accept?
q4.answer: We accept bank transfers in euros (EUR). The quarterly plan automatically saves you €150 compared to three monthly payments - €1,185 instead of €1,335.

hook.p1: When a customer types 'plumber near me', 'dentist Sofia', or 'accountant Lozenets' into Google, the top 3 results on the map take roughly 75% of the clicks. Everything below that first screen is, in practice, invisible. SEO optimization in Sofia is the discipline that decides whether your business is in those 3 spots or not.
hook.p2: Most Sofia business owners we meet have tried one of two things: a Google Ads campaign that drained their budget the moment it was paused, or a generic marketing agency that 'did SEO' but couldn't explain what actually changed. This page is the long version of what real SEO optimization for a local Sofia business looks like — the pillars, the timelines, the signals Google actually weighs, and the specific mistakes that keep most companies stuck at positions 10-20 on the map.

whatItMeans.title: What SEO optimization really means for a Sofia business
whatItMeans.p1: SEO optimization is the ongoing work of convincing Google that your business is the most relevant, most trusted answer to a specific local search. For a dentist in Lozenets, that search is 'dentist Lozenets' or 'dentist near me' when the user is walking past Paradise Center. For a plumber in Mladost, it's 'plumber Mladost' at 7pm on a Sunday when a pipe has just burst.
whatItMeans.p2: What people call 'SEO' on Google nationally and 'local SEO' on Google Maps are two different sports. National SEO is a slow, content-heavy game played against thousands of pages. Local SEO — the only kind that matters for a Sofia business with a physical address or service area — is a compact game played against 10-20 direct competitors in your specific neighborhood. The signals Google uses are different, the timelines are shorter, and the ROI is dramatically higher.
whatItMeans.p3: SEO optimization in Sofia, done properly, touches three surfaces at once: your Google Business Profile (GBP, formerly Google My Business), your website, and the web of third-party signals around you — directories, reviews, mentions, citations. If even one of these is weak, the other two cannot carry the ranking. Most Sofia businesses we audit fix one and wonder why nothing moves.

whyGenericFails.title: Why generic SEO agencies fail Sofia businesses
whyGenericFails.p1: The typical marketing agency in Sofia sells 'a bit of everything': social media, Google Ads, web design, a content plan, and SEO as a bullet in the proposal. That model makes sense for agencies — recurring retainers are easier when you stack services. It makes no sense for a local business that only needs customers from a 3-5 kilometer radius.
whyGenericFails.p2: Three specific ways generic agencies fail Sofia clients:
reasons: They chase national keywords. A dental clinic in Studentski grad does not need to rank for 'dental implants Bulgaria'. It needs to rank for 'dentist Studentski grad' and 'dental clinic Lozenets'. Those are easier, cheaper, and convert at a far higher rate.
They ignore the Google Business Profile. In the 2026 ranking landscape, GBP is 60-70% of the work. Website-only SEO in Sofia is like building a beautiful storefront in a closed mall.

They don't measure what matters. Impressions and 'traffic to site' are vanity metrics in local SEO. What matters is: position on the map for the primary query, profile calls, direction requests, and profile-to-website clicks. If your monthly report doesn't show those four numbers, it's not a local SEO report.

pillars.title: The 3 pillars of SEO optimization in Sofia
pillars.intro: Every SEO optimization project Atlas Fold takes on in Sofia rests on three pillars. Miss any of them and the ranking stalls.

gbp.title: Google Business Profile optimization
gbp.p1: Your Google Business Profile is where 70%+ of local discovery happens. A correctly optimized profile in Sofia means: primary category matching your single most-searched service (not a vague umbrella like 'business consultant'), additional categories layered in precisely, service area mapped to the neighborhoods you actually serve — not the entire city of Sofia — opening hours marked as 'open 24 hours' only if that's true, business description written with the primary keyword in the first 250 characters, photos geotagged and uploaded on a schedule, and a steady stream of posts that Google treats as freshness signals.
gbp.p2: The mistake we see most often on Sofia profiles: a business picks one primary category ('restaurant'), doesn't add the 3-4 secondary categories Google allows ('Italian restaurant', 'pizza restaurant', 'family restaurant', 'terrace restaurant'), and then competes against the entire 'restaurant' universe in Sofia instead of the narrower, more winnable slices.

onPage.title: On-page SEO — the foundation of the website
onPage.intro: On-page SEO is every signal your own website sends to Google. For a local Sofia business, the non-negotiables are:
items: A title tag in the format 'Best [service] [neighborhood] — [business name]' that Google reads as the page topic. Yes, it's longer than 60 characters. Ignore the outdated 60-character rule — Google uses the full string for relevance, even if only part of it is displayed in the snippet.
Exactly one H1 per page, naming the primary category and the city.
H2s covering the secondary categories and the 4-5 most important services, so the page demonstrates topical coverage.

A NAP block (Name, Address, Phone) in the footer as plain crawlable text — not an image — that matches the GBP string character-for-character. 'ul.' vs 'ulitsa', 'EOOD' vs 'Ltd', '+359' vs '0' — any mismatch dilutes trust.
LocalBusiness and FAQ schema in the page source, so Google reads the structured version of your NAP, services, hours, and questions directly.
Page speed under 2.5s LCP and a CLS under 0.1. Sofia mobile 4G is not American fiber — sites that bloat over 3MB on the first screen lose mobile rankings.
onPage.outro: Each of these compounds. Fixing 2 of 6 moves nothing. Fixing all 6 is what takes a Sofia business from position 12 to position 3.

citations.title: Local citations & authority signals
citations.p1: A citation is any third-party mention of your business across the web with a consistent NAP. For a Sofia business, the relevant citation surfaces are: bgmaps.com, navimaps.bg, pozvanete.bg, ciela.net/business, 0700.bg, profesionalisti.bg, industry-specific portals (e.g., zdravni-portali.bg for dental clinics, autoservize.bg for auto repair), Bulgarian chamber directories, and cross-referenced mentions on local news portals.
citations.p2: The quality bar matters more than the quantity. 40 high-trust, perfectly consistent citations beat 400 low-quality scraped ones. Google cross-checks NAP strings across citations when it decides how 'real' a local business is. A single inconsistency — the business name appearing as 'Atlas Fold EOOD' on one directory and 'Atlas Fold Ltd' on another — sends a confusion signal.
citations.p3: Beyond citations, authority signals include: contextually relevant backlinks from Bulgarian sites in your industry, partnerships with local suppliers or associations, sponsorships of neighborhood events that generate press mentions, and reviews on Google, Facebook, and industry-specific platforms. The goal is not 'more links'. The goal is a coherent, believable local presence that Google can verify from multiple angles.

measure.title: How we measure SEO optimization results
measure.intro: We report four numbers every two weeks:
items: Average position on Google Maps for your primary search term.
Market share in the 3-pack — the percentage of relevant local searches where your business appears in the top 3.
Profile calls and direction requests, pulled directly from Google Business Profile insights.
Website clicks originating from the profile.
measure.outro: Impressions and raw traffic are in the appendix, not the first page. If the four numbers above don't improve month over month, the strategy is wrong and we say so.

steps.title: 1. Free audit
steps.body: We screen your GBP, website, and top 3 local competitors. You get a written snapshot of every gap, even if you never hire us.

steps.title: 2. Strategy

howSearchesWork.title: How local searches actually work in Lozenets
howSearchesWork.intro: Three search patterns dominate Lozenets queries:

patterns.label: '[Service] Lozenets'
patterns.body: 'dentist Lozenets', 'café Lozenets', 'yoga Lozenets'. Deliberate neighborhood search. High intent.

patterns.label: '[Service] near me'
patterns.body: User currently in Lozenets or driving toward Paradise Center, James Bourchier metro, or South Park. Google uses the phone's location to return a local 3-pack.

patterns.label: '[Landmark/street] [service]'
patterns.body: 'Café near James Bourchier', 'dentist near VMA'. Proximity-to-landmark search. More common among older residents and expatriates.

howSearchesWork.outro: For each of these, Google's local algorithm weighs three factors roughly in this order: relevance (does the profile match the query), distance (how close is the business to the searcher), and prominence (how trusted is the business — reviews, citations, profile completeness). Most Lozenets clients we audit have invisible relevance — incorrect primary category, no services listed, generic business description — and weak prominence. Distance they can't change. Relevance and prominence we fix in 4-6 weeks.

landmarks.title: The Lozenets streets and landmarks your profile should name
landmarks.intro: Lozenets customers reference a specific set of landmarks and streets when they talk to Google or to each other:
landmarks.outro: Your Google Business Profile description, website area page, and FAQ should reference at least 3-4 of these — not as keyword stuffing, but as natural local context. Google cross-references entities in its knowledge graph. When your site mentions 'close to South Park and Paradise Center', Google has more confidence you are actually in Lozenets.

proximity.title: Why proximity alone is not enough
proximity.p1: Business owners in Lozenets tell us: 'I'm right next to Paradise Center, why am I not showing up?' Proximity is one of three ranking factors, not the only one. A profile 200m from the searcher but with 15 reviews, no category, and inconsistent citations will lose to a profile 800m away with 280 reviews, 15 photos uploaded this month, and a dialed-in GBP description.
proximity.p2: Distance is also relative. Google uses a 'centroid of intent' — for searches without proximity clues, it weights businesses closer to the neighborhood center, not to the searcher. Businesses on the edge of Lozenets (near Hladilnika or James Bourchier metro) often need stronger prominence signals to compensate. The fix is always the same: win on relevance, win on prominence, accept distance as a constant, and watch the map ranking climb.
